tagline: A dual lactate-pyruvate fluorescent sensing system as a low-cost grassroots pre-screening tool for cancer risk
summary: PyrLac Glow reads the Warburg effect directly: two allosteric fluorescent biosensors, built by inserting YFP into the transcription regulators PdhR (pyruvate) and LldR (L-lactate), report the concentrations and the ratio of the two metabolites through a dual-lock mechanism. The project targets a specific structural gap in Chinese cancer screening - CT, endoscopy and liquid biopsy are accurate but inaccessible at grassroots level, while conventional serum tumour markers are cheap but not specific enough - with fewer than 10% of patients diagnosed early. The team ran 16 in-depth interviews across clinical practice, research, industry, public health, insurance, education and engineering, plus two questionnaires (208 and 113 valid responses), organised into five sequential stages each answering one question and each closing with a 'What we changed' statement. The biomarker architecture, the product category, the deployment scenarios, the hardware scope, the software permission model and the outreach strategy all changed as a direct result.
awards: Best Integrated Human Practices nominee (High School)

dry.frameworks: A multi-evidence computational screening workflow to choose YFP insertion breakpoints in each sensor, combining conserved domain annotation, static structural rigidity assessment, physicochemical profiling, molecular docking and molecular dynamics. For PdhR they built a five-feature weighted scoring model that scores and ranks every residue along the full-length sequence, with C-terminal oligomerisation residues included but penalised by steric hindrance and conformational tolerance terms, and high-scoring candidates still requiring manual secondary verification. For LldR they started from experimentally validated insertion hotspots reported in patent CN113004420A rather than scoring blind.
dry.dataviz: An interactive five-stage IHP architecture diagram with collapsible numbered nodes, a four-group stakeholder classification map (end screening users, clinical practitioners, industry and technical developers, public health and policy regulators) with each group's concerns attached, and a closed-loop summary figure pairing core achievements, key limitations and future plans.
dry.datascience: Questionnaire analysis with explicit sampling-bias reporting: 78.37% female respondents, 91.83% urban, income above 20,000 RMB per year, and the team states outright that the sample under-covers rural, low-income and elderly male populations and makes those groups a target for later outreach. Hardware requirement data were gathered in a second, deliberately non-overlapping questionnaire. Apo-to-holo conformational modelling explains the sensing mechanism: hinge flexibility distorts the embedded YFP beta-barrel for low basal fluorescence, and ligand-induced contraction rigidifies the hinge so YFP refolds and fluorescence rises.
dry.software: A modular data processing backbone designed with a former Microsoft vice president: signal acquisition, data buffering, data quality verification, sample labelling, separate processing pipelines for CMOS sensors and photoresistors, data storage and visualisation, with anonymous sample IDs, full retention of both raw and processed data, spreadsheet export at prototype stage, and module decoupling so sensors or verification algorithms can be upgraded without rebuilding the system.
techniques: allosteric transcription-factor biosensor engineering (YFP insertion into PdhR and LldR)
standard curve construction with biological and technical replicates
POCT prototype design with disposable preloaded cartridges

good.publicEngagement: Outreach is unusually self-critical for a high school team. They produced two differentiated brochures (a children's version with illustrations and simple language, and a systematic middle/high school version covering experimental principles), ran an activity at Suzhou Science and Technology Town Foreign Language High School for about 60 ninth-graders using a Kahoot quiz to build the prerequisite cell-biology concepts before introducing the project, and a themed lacquer-fan creation exercise so students re-expressed the science visually. A shopping-mall event reached a broad cross-section but returned only three completed questionnaires from high foot traffic, and the team published that failure with a diagnosis: a mall suits short accessible outreach rather than detailed survey collection, their material distribution lacked interactive elements and 'often raised suspicion', and next time they would lead with their school and iGEM identity to build trust and standardise the introduction between team members. For a professional audience they rewrote the talk, cutting health-management content and expanding the Warburg effect, dual-biomarker and protein-expression material, then coded the questions received into knowledge and attitude dimensions. A 30-student pre-study tested whether a single outreach event can shift awareness at all.
good.ihp: Bist-China's five-stage structure forces each stakeholder round to produce a change, and the changes are substantial rather than cosmetic. The single biggest one is the biomarker architecture: the initial design used lactate alone, and a pathologist at a hospital in Zhuhai, Guangdong told them that many benign physiological fluctuations produce fluorescent signals resembling malignant signatures, so a single-marker assay 'would not be clinically accepted for large-scale pre-screening' - the team abandoned the single-lactate scheme and adopted combined lactate-pyruvate detection, making specificity and anti-interference the primary optimisation goals. Dr Feiran Han (Director of the Institute of Science and Technology, LC-Bio) then confirmed dual-marker feasibility but told them two markers were the right number for a high-school project because a third would dilute validation depth, so they locked the panel at two and built standardised SOPs with replicates and standard curves converting fluorescence into metabolite concentrations. Stage 1 produced a product-category change: cancer survivors described the 1-2 year early warning window missed through fear of positive results, and oncologist Dr Wu Qing explained that fewer than 10% of cases are caught early and that clinicians fear false positives triggering public panic - crucially, Dr Wu partially contradicted the patient interviews, saying patients often refuse screening not because of cost but because they do not know how to interpret an ambiguous result, which the team records as shifting their attention 'from reducing cost to designing unambiguous result communication'. PyrLac Glow was repositioned from a diagnostic device to a risk pre-screening tool that refers high-risk individuals onward, with an explicit trade-off rule carried forward into Stage 2: prioritise reducing missed diagnoses while tolerating interpretable false positives. Staff at Cuiyuan Community Health Service Center in Xihu District, Hangzhou killed the household self-test idea outright - community centres have no high-precision instruments or full-time pathologists, send samples out for 3-7 day report cycles, have overloaded general practitioners, and will only adopt after official medical device certification - so the team abandoned household positioning and fixed three deployment scenarios. Prof. Ying Xiao of Shanghai University of Traditional Chinese Medicine changed the report interface: avoid absolute 'cancer / no cancer' conclusions and use physical-examination-style wording (metabolic abnormality, potential risk, re-test recommended), and treat constitution information as auxiliary explanation only since using it to reduce false positives remains a hypothesis. The most consequential safety change came from Erika Ferreri (Bellevue College, Washington State Department of Health, 21 years in medical laboratory education), who found the prototype could output cancer risk conclusions directly to ordinary users: the team re-scoped it as a bench-side research prototype for trained professionals, stripped risk judgments from the device interface so it reports only raw concentrations and quality-control status, added unique sample IDs, full raw-data retention and error-triggered automatic re-testing, separated the operator backend from the doctor and patient report interface, and deferred patient-facing reports until clinical validation - 'this transformed the prototype from an open prototype to a controlled medical research device'. A mechanical manufacturing chairman stopped them wasting the season on shell appearance and tolerances, imposing a core-function-first rule and forward design from commercially available standard components. Commercially, an AIA insurance specialist's view that insurers will not lead on immature technology and barely accept results from private organisations directly removed insurance as a primary channel, redirecting the strategy to corporate physical examinations and public medical screening; a corporate HR director with a 500-RMB-per-employee annual budget set a 200-RMB consumable cost target and added the third deployment scenario the team had missed; an IVD company chairman located the real gap between student prototype and product in batch stability and clinical validation rather than principle verification, turning a 5% to 15% CV benchmark into a quality-control design target. Most tellingly, they record advice they declined with reasons: they rejected educational psychologist Margaret's suggestion to invest in short-video platforms because a high-school team lacks the resources for continuous content production and the compliance capacity for medical-adjacent content, substituting a school health-curriculum lecture series and printed booklet; and they only partially accepted Erika Ferreri's multi-language recommendation, supporting Chinese and English now and deferring the rest. They also resolved a genuine disagreement among the iGEM teams they consulted about whether to validate biology before building hardware by choosing a middle path with a stated rule - hardware parameters must be re-validated against final Stage 2 experimental parameters before freezing.
good.realWorld: The need is quantified against the system that would have to absorb the product: roughly 50% of cancers worldwide diagnosed at advanced stage, fewer than 10% of Chinese patients diagnosed early, 3-7 day report turnaround at community centres with no on-site pathologist, and 58.65% of their own 208 respondents unfamiliar with or completely unaware of early screening - from which they draw the sharpest framing in the project, that the bottleneck is the public 'does not know screening is needed' rather than refuses screening. Cost targets come from stakeholders rather than guesswork and are triangulated across two independent sources: public expectation of under 1,000 RMB per test from the questionnaire, and a per-person threshold of 200 RMB from the corporate HR budget of about 500 RMB per employee per year. Hardware constraints are equally specific: results within 30 minutes, wireless transmission to a phone (62.83% called this very necessary), disposable preloaded disc cartridges, single-use safety (76.11% support), and professional-scenario priority. The regulatory path is laid out concretely - medical device registration and official certification as the precondition for community adoption, POCT specifications for the operating manual, and prospective clinical trials enrolling high-risk populations with 1-2 years of follow-up to establish consistency and positive and negative predictive value, with a staged roadmap of top-tier hospital pilot, data-driven validation, then guideline endorsement, and a stated commercialisation horizon of 3-5 years (5-10 for widespread adoption). No SDG is claimed anywhere on the wiki, which is a genuine gap for a project that frames itself in public-health terms. The limitations section is honest and specific: laboratory validation only with no large clinical sample set for threshold training, no medical device qualification, the science communication plan still at design stage, and the questionnaire sample biased toward urban populations. Future work is committed to a clinical-pilot-first route before any market expansion.

gemsTakeaway: Record the advice you declined and why, alongside the advice you took: Bist-China's refusals (short-video outreach beyond their compliance capacity, multi-language deferred to commercialisation) and its openly flagged stakeholder contradictions are what prove the engagement was deliberation rather than endorsement-collection.
